name: epiAneufinder / pyEpiAneufinder
tagline: A depth profile is corrected for bias, segmented, and classified relative to the cell.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Bin and GC-correct scATAC depth, filter unreliable cells and bins, and form cluster pseudobulk profiles.

steps.title: Propose
steps.text: Recursively search eligible split positions for the strongest Anderson–Darling (AD) difference, respecting minimum segment sizes.

steps.title: Test
steps.text: Accept a proposed split only when local and genome-pool global permutation tests meet the configured criterion; recurse on accepted segments.

steps.title: Assign
steps.text: Use the original pyEpi assign_gainloss_new with genome-wide fitted best_s to assign relative per-cell states on the resulting segments.

steps.title: Explore separately
steps.text: The app’s optional adjacent-segment merging and re-calling is an exploratory transformation, not an implicit step of baseline segmentation.

example.title: A candidate boundary across many bins
example.setup: Illustratively, four consecutive stretches each contain many bins; their corrected mean depths are approximately 10, 11, 5 and 5.
steps: Search eligible positions in the full bin-level profile, subject to size constraints.
A split near the change from the second to third stretch is a candidate; local and genome-pool permutations determine acceptance.
If accepted, recursively examine resulting segments, then fit best_s and assign relative states.
example.interpretation: The block means alone cannot determine whether a split passes either test; an accepted lower segment is a relative signal, not an absolute copy count.

available: Existing pyEpi binned depth and relative calls
needed: Counting-unit and bin provenance
Independent truth or realistic simulations
adaptation.first_experiment: Inspect low-depth segments across coverage thresholds and record seeds for any subsampling.
adaptation.success: Report stability and uncertainty against independent evidence, without treating agreement as truth.

cautions: Sparse accessibility can resemble loss.
Category 0 means relative loss, not zero copies.
MCF10-A is a nonmalignant development sample, not a diploid label.

name: Copy-scAT
tagline: Chromosome-scale scATAC coverage is normalized and assessed for broad and focal alterations.

steps.title: Bin
steps.text: Count fragments in genomic bins for each cell.

steps.title: Filter
steps.text: Remove low-quality cells and bins that are mostly zero.

steps.title: Normalize
steps.text: Adjust for library size and relevant baseline effects.

steps.title: Assess
steps.text: Evaluate chromosome-arm coverage for broad gains and losses; use a separate focal amplification analysis.

example.title: Arm-level comparison
example.setup: Illustrative normalized bins on one arm are 0.7, 0.8, 0.7, versus a baseline near 1.
steps: Aggregate the arm’s usable bins.
Compare its signal with the chosen within-sample baseline.
Check whether a narrow peak warrants separate focal analysis.
example.interpretation: The broad decrease is a candidate relative loss, subject to coverage and baseline checks.

needed: Compatible fragment inputs and matching bin definitions
Documented baseline settings
adaptation.first_experiment: Run a small matched-cell comparison after confirming input availability.
adaptation.success: Describe arm-level agreement and discordance by coverage, without calling either tool truth.

cautions: Default resolution is coarse and focal analysis is distinct.
No validated absolute or biallelic deletion call follows from low signal.
Fragments were not established as available in this workspace.

name: Alleloscope
tagline: Pool SNP allele counts across cells and candidate regions to estimate haplotype imbalance.

steps.title: Define regions
steps.text: Provide candidate genomic regions and allele counts at informative SNPs.

steps.title: Phase
steps.text: Estimate SNP haplotype orientation jointly across cells using an expectation-maximization procedure.

steps.title: Pool
steps.text: Aggregate oriented alleles within each region for more informative regional counts.

steps.title: Estimate
steps.text: Estimate cell-level major-haplotype proportions and combine with relative coverage to assess allele states and confidence.

example.title: Regional imbalance
example.setup: Illustratively, phased observations in one region total 18 reads on one haplotype and 6 on the other.
steps: Orient SNP alleles consistently before pooling.
The pooled fraction is 18/24 = 0.75.
Compare this regional imbalance with relative depth and uncertainty.
example.interpretation: The signal is consistent with imbalance; it does not by itself determine an integer genotype.

available: AT site observations and relative depth exist
needed: SNP-level counts and region definitions
Verified phase and preferably matched DNA segmentation
adaptation.first_experiment: Audit whether SNP-level counts and phase can be reconstructed for one region.
adaptation.success: Quantify usable sites and uncertainty before attempting a regional comparison.

cautions: Unobserved alleles are missing evidence, not zero copies.
Phase errors or cell mixtures can distort pooled fractions.
Matched DNA segmentation is recommended for scATAC.

name: Numbat-multiome
tagline: A joint probabilistic model combines reference-normalized ATAC depth and phased SNP alleles along chromosomes.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Supply raw bin-by-cell ATAC counts, genomic bins, normalized ATAC reference and phased SNP-level allele counts.

steps.title: Model
steps.text: Use a Poisson-lognormal coverage model and a beta-binomial phased allele-count model to score candidate joint states.

steps.title: Connect
steps.text: A hidden Markov model (HMM) shares information across neighboring bins and models state transitions.

steps.title: Pool
steps.text: Iterative clone-aware pooling improves estimates and returns state probabilities and clones.

example.title: Joint evidence
example.setup: Imagine a region with normalized depth near 0.6 and phased counts 18 versus 6.
steps: Compare depth against a defensible ATAC reference.
Score allele imbalance using the phased counts and their uncertainty.
Combine both signals with neighboring bins in the HMM.
example.interpretation: A loss-like state may gain support, but this hypothetical input is not a tool result or proof of absolute copy number.

available: Existing ATAC depth and site observations
Published ATAC-bin mode is a relevant comparator
needed: Suitable ATAC reference
Compatible raw fragment counts, bin geometry, phased SNP-level counts and verified phase continuity
adaptation.first_experiment: Audit inputs and reference suitability before a small ATAC-bin feasibility run.
adaptation.success: Demonstrate input compatibility and report posterior uncertainty against independent evidence.

cautions: No suitable normal reference is established here; MCF10-A is not assumed diploid.
Current pyEpi pipeline uses AD segmentation, not this HMM.
Missing alleles and uncertain phase restrict power; ATAC 0:0 sensitivity is unvalidated here.

name: CopyKAT
tagline: Smooth ordered gene expression to identify broad relative copy-number patterns in scRNA-seq.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Order RNA genes genomically, apply a variance-stabilizing Freeman–Tukey transformation, and smooth outliers with a polynomial dynamic linear model.

steps.title: Reference
steps.text: Use clustering and Gaussian-mixture criteria to infer a putative diploid reference; this assumption can fail.

steps.title: Segment
steps.text: Apply Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo segmentation to relative expression, then merge segments using Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests.

steps.title: Classify
steps.text: Use the resulting broad profiles and normal-enrichment/mixture criteria to group cells and explore subclones.

example.title: Expression pattern
example.setup: Hypothetically, a sequence of genes has normalized expression near 0.7 compared with a putative reference of 1.
steps: Order the genes and smooth local expression.
Identify a sustained change across a broad interval.
Compare the interval and cells with the inferred reference.
example.interpretation: The change is a candidate RNA-derived relative alteration; regulated expression could also contribute.

available: Relative ATAC profiles provide a development baseline
needed: Compatible RNA expression matrix and gene coordinates
Defensible reference strategy
adaptation.first_experiment: Study reference sensitivity on a separate compatible RNA dataset before transferring any concept.
adaptation.success: Report how inferred baseline and broad calls change with reference choice.

cautions: RNA expression is not ATAC fragment depth; direct input substitution is invalid.
A putative diploid group is an inference, not verified normal truth.
Smoothing can obscure focal events.

name: inferCNV
tagline: Compare genomically smoothed RNA expression in cells with a chosen reference.

steps.title: Order
steps.text: Provide gene expression, gene order and cell annotations.

steps.title: Reference
steps.text: Estimate expected expression from selected reference cells or a defined alternative.

steps.title: Smooth
steps.text: Denoise expression and smooth along ordered genes to reveal broad patterns.

steps.title: Infer
steps.text: Optionally apply an HMM: i3 models loss, neutral and gain; i6 estimates six state emissions using simulated expression spike-ins based on reference cells.

example.title: Reference comparison
example.setup: Suppose five neighboring genes average 0.8 relative to selected reference cells.
steps: Normalize each cell and compare gene expression to the reference.
Smooth across nearby genes.
Inspect the broad deviation and optionally infer HMM states.
example.interpretation: A persistent decrease is a candidate RNA signal, not evidence of an absolute deletion.

available: ATAC bins and relative pyEpi calls
needed: Gene expression and gene positions
Reference annotations with explicit assumptions
adaptation.first_experiment: Test how changing a reference affects a compatible RNA example; document what transfers conceptually.
adaptation.success: Show reference sensitivity separately from independent validation.

cautions: ATAC accessibility and RNA expression have different biases; do not run directly on ATAC bins.
A cell cluster is not automatically a normal reference.
Smoothing cannot turn absent evidence into a measured region.

name: CaSpER
tagline: Combine multiscale RNA expression and allele-frequency patterns to identify candidate alterations.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Obtain RNA expression and allele-read profiles with genomic positions.

steps.title: Smooth
steps.text: Apply recursive median filtering at several scales to expression and B-allele-frequency (BAF) shift signals.

steps.title: Segment
steps.text: At each expression scale, a five-state HMM segments the smoothed expression profile.

steps.title: Integrate
steps.text: Filter candidate segments for concordant BAF shifts; a Gaussian mixture model helps set the shift threshold.

example.title: Two RNA signals
example.setup: Suppose a region’s expression is low relative to a reference and its observed alleles are 18 versus 6.
steps: Smooth nearby expression values at a chosen scale.
Summarize allele-frequency shifts across the region.
Compare where the two candidate signals overlap.
example.interpretation: Concordant signals can motivate follow-up; allelic expression and sparse reads can produce misleading shifts.

needed: Compatible RNA expression and RNA allele inputs
Defined reference and smoothing choices
adaptation.first_experiment: Use the multiscale idea to inspect stability across ATAC resolutions without substituting the RNA model.
adaptation.success: Record which candidates persist across scales and where allele evidence is missing.

cautions: CaSpER is an RNA method; transferring its emissions to ATAC needs separate validation.
Allelic expression bias can mimic imbalance.
A low signal is not proof of a homozygous deletion.
The RNA HMM includes a homozygous-deletion state, but its existence does not establish detection in this ATAC workflow.

name: HoneyBADGER
tagline: Use probabilistic genomic models of RNA expression and allele observations to infer candidate CNV and LOH.

steps.title: Cluster
steps.text: Cluster cells using smoothed lesser-allele fractions, split into groups and pool their observations.

steps.title: Find regions
steps.text: Apply an HMM to pooled lesser-allele fractions to identify candidate CNV or LOH regions.

steps.title: Score cells
steps.text: Use a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate per-cell posterior probabilities for each candidate region, incorporating expression and alleles.

steps.title: Recurse
steps.text: Cluster cells by posterior probabilities, split into putative subclones, and repeat until no further subclones are found.

example.title: Sparse RNA alleles
example.setup: Imagine a region with reduced expression and 18 versus 6 allele reads across informative SNPs.
steps: Order expression and allele evidence along the genome.
Model persistence of candidate states across nearby observations.
Inspect posterior support and region-level evidence.
example.interpretation: A region may support a candidate alteration, while RNA-specific biases and uncertain baselines remain plausible.

needed: RNA expression and allele matrices for the actual method
A separately justified ATAC observation model for any adaptation
adaptation.first_experiment: Prototype separate depth and allele evidence displays, including missingness, before proposing any joint model.
adaptation.success: Retain calibrated uncertainty and distinguish absence of observations from evidence of balance.

cautions: RNA-based emissions cannot simply be applied to ATAC.
Pooling can mask heterogeneous cells.
Missing-data behavior requires further source audit.

name: XClone
tagline: Model RNA read-depth and phased allelic signals separately, then combine their state evidence.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Build gene-by-cell expression and allele count matrices and select reference cells.

steps.title: Phase
steps.text: Orient allele counts through local and broader phasing steps.

steps.title: Model
steps.text: Fit separate expression and allele mixture models; the phased allele module uses a beta-binomial likelihood. Smooth state probabilities along the genome using an HMM and across related cells.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Combine module outputs to obtain candidate allele-specific copy-number state probabilities.

example.title: Complementary evidence
example.setup: A hypothetical region has expression ratio 0.7 and phased RNA counts 18 versus 6.
steps: The expression module scores the lower ratio.
The allele module evaluates imbalance and its uncertainty.
Combine the module evidence while retaining each separate result.
example.interpretation: Concordance strengthens a candidate relative alteration but does not independently validate an integer state.

needed: RNA expression and allele inputs for XClone
Verified phase continuity and a defensible reference
adaptation.first_experiment: Visualize ATAC depth and allelic evidence side by side with explicit missing-data masks.
adaptation.success: Find cases of concordance and disagreement without treating either signal as ground truth.

cautions: XClone is designed for RNA, so its noise model requires validation before any ATAC adaptation.
Neighbor smoothing can mix biologically distinct cells.
No observed alleles cannot be treated as balanced.

name: CHISEL
tagline: Phase SNP blocks across cells and jointly cluster DNA depth and allele balance to infer allele-specific states.

steps.title: Count
steps.text: Derive read-depth ratios and SNP allele counts from barcoded single-cell DNA sequencing.

steps.title: Phase
steps.text: Orient SNP blocks using information shared across cells.

steps.title: Cluster
steps.text: Jointly cluster depth and allele fractions to identify recurrent genomic and cellular patterns.

steps.title: Assign
steps.text: Infer allele-specific integer states and clones using ploidy and reference assumptions.

example.title: Two depth and allele patterns
example.setup: In an illustrative DNA region, one cell has depth ratio 0.7 and phased counts 18 versus 6.
steps: Build genomic bins and phase informative SNPs across cells.
Compare depth and allele fractions with patterns from other cells.
Assign candidate states only under a specified reference and ploidy model.
example.interpretation: The pattern suggests an imbalance candidate; exact integer assignment depends on the model and assumptions.

available: Relative ATAC depth and site observations
needed: Compatible DNA BAM and SNP data for CHISEL
Independent calibration and validated phasing for any ATAC-inspired approach
adaptation.first_experiment: Audit whether phase orientation could be estimated across cells without assuming clone labels.
adaptation.success: Measure phase consistency and uncertainty on independent controls or simulations.

cautions: DNA read-depth emissions do not automatically transfer to accessibility.
Default mode uses a matched normal; no-normal mode still has assumptions.
Relative category 0 cannot supply absolute zero-copy input.

name: signals
tagline: Phase alleles across low-coverage DNA cells, then infer haplotype states with an HMM.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Provide total integer DNA copy-number bins and per-cell haplotype-block allele counts.

steps.title: Phase
steps.text: Use patterns of gains and losses across cells to orient alleles.

steps.title: Model
steps.text: Use an HMM to infer allele-specific states along the genome given total copy number.

steps.title: Report
steps.text: Return haplotype-specific states and LOH-related labels for each cell and bin.

example.title: Conditioning on total copy number
example.setup: Suppose a DNA bin has independently inferred total CN 2 and phased counts 18 versus 6.
steps: Provide the integer total CN and oriented block counts.
Compare candidate haplotype states under the allele model.
Use neighboring bins to inform the HMM state.
example.interpretation: An imbalanced candidate can be assessed only conditional on the supplied CN and phase; the counts alone do not fix a genotype.

available: ATAC site observations and relative categories
needed: Independently justified integer total CN
Compatible haplotype block counts and validated phase
adaptation.first_experiment: Check whether any independent DNA-derived total CN is available before considering this comparator.
adaptation.success: Explicitly document input provenance and assess uncertainty from upstream CN and phase.

cautions: The existing loss/base/gain categories are not integer total copy number.
A-Hom or B-Hom indicates one allele lost, not necessarily both.
This DNA method is not validated for the current ATAC data.
